leads.name: Sakon-no-Sakura, Kyoto Imperial Palace (Shishinden)

location.neighbourhood: Shishinden courtyard, Kyoto Imperial Palace, Kamigyo-ku

leads.reason: Fails the genuinely-old bar, not a count or evidence problem: this is a ceremonial specimen that has been replanted in the same spot repeatedly since the Heian period whenever the previous tree died or the palace burned and was rebuilt. The Kunaicho's own tree page (kyoto-gosho.kunaicho.go.jp/en/tree/4E1) and Japanese-language sources agree the current cherry was planted in 1998, making it roughly 28 years old as of 2026, not an ancient tree. Historically significant as a site and a tradition (first written record of a storm felling its predecessor dates to 874 CE), genuinely photogenic, but the living specimen itself does not clear the bar. Could work as an illustration of the site's history inside another tree's story, never as its own collectible entry.

leads.name: Ukon-no-Tachibana, Kyoto Imperial Palace (Shishinden)

location.neighbourhood: Shishinden courtyard, Kyoto Imperial Palace, Kamigyo-ku

leads.reason: Same problem as Sakon-no-Sakura: a ceremonial specimen replanted repeatedly through history whenever it died or the palace was rebuilt elsewhere, most recently referenced as replanted circa 959 CE in tradition but with no continuous individual tree since. Kunaicho's own page (tree/4E2) and Japanese sources describe it as symbolically eternal (the tachibana is evergreen, chosen precisely to represent permanence) rather than physically ancient. Fails the genuinely-old bar for the same reason as its paired cherry.

leads.name: Mukuroji (soapberry) of Manosaka entrance, Kyoto Gyoen

location.neighbourhood: Near Manosaka-guchi, east side of Kyoto Gyoen, Kamigyo-ku

leads.reason: Kamigyo Ward 'Pride Tree', but the smallest of the group checked this pass (12.5m height, 2.14m girth). Single-sourced, no age. Lowest priority of the Gyoen leads.

leads.name: 遂龍松 (Yuryu-matsu / Reclining Dragon Pine), Zenko-ji, Nishikyo-ku
leads.reason: Register candidate (japan-bunkacho.json) within 80m of already-published kyo_001 'The Reclining Dragon Pine', which is also a National Natural Monument pine at Zenko-ji with the same Japanese name. Almost certainly the same tree already on the site. Not re-verified or re-published; recorded here so a future pass does not re-research it from a register hit alone. Check kyo_001's exact coordinates and sources before assuming this is a genuinely separate specimen. CONFIRMED 2026-08-23: kyo_001 ("The Reclining Dragon Pine") stands at 34.93828,135.6449362, about 15-20m from this register point, same species (Japanese White Pine), same story (a nationally designated natural monument pine trained to grow horizontally, named by a 19th-century official). Marked duplicate rather than re-published.

blocked.name: 遂龍松 (Yuryu-matsu / Reclining Dragon Pine), Zenko-ji, Nishikyo-ku
blocked.reason: DUPLICATE of published kyo_001, The Reclining Dragon Pine: 17 m away, same species, same address at Yoshimine-dera in Oharano. The register glyphs 遂龍松 are an OCR slip for 遊龍松, 'playing dragon', which is what kyo_001's own story already calls it, and the file's 'Zenko-ji' is an alternate reading of 善峯寺. Never publish; it would put one tree on the site twice.

shipped.reason: Published as kyo_015, 2026-08-12, once HELD 2026-08-11/12 on a shared placeholder coordinate identical to kyo_017's. Resolved by looking up Seisho-mon gate's real position via OSM/Nominatim (35.0258332, 135.7610189) rather than guessing; the tree stands southwest of that gate per an independent web source, so the gate itself is used as an honest gate-area estimate, matching the convention already used for kyo_011.

shipped.name: Camphor of Shimodachiuri Gate, Kyoto Gyoen
shipped.reason: Published as kyo_017, 2026-08-12, once HELD for the same shared-coordinate reason as kyo_015. Resolved via OSM/Nominatim, which has this gate itself tagged as a building at 35.0195774, 135.7595584, matching the story's own 'grows just inside Shimodachiuri-gomon'. Species corrected to the site's canonical 'Camphor Tree (Cinnamomum camphora)'. Note: this coordinate sits only ~25m from the already-published kyo_011 (Demizu-guchi hackberry)'s own coordinate, despite both trees' stories placing them a short walk apart in the same southwest corner of the park. kyo_011's own pin (already flagged location_precision: approximate) may itself be imprecise; worth a future pass with stronger evidence rather than changed on this one's coattails.
